Guidance for school boards on good decision making

If a parent or caregiver is unhappy with a decision made by a school board, they have the right to complain to the Chief Ombudsman. Many complaints received by the Ombudsman are about disciplinary issues – and focus on situations where the student has been suspended, excluded, or expelled.
 
This video features Chief Ombudsman Peter Boshier and Newlands Intermediate staff members giving an overview on how to take the right steps for good decision making. It outlines the decision-making process, who can help guide school boards, and where to find more resources.

The Kiingitanga & Chief Ombudsman Summer Internship Programme 2022

The Kiingitanga & Chief Ombudsman Summer Internship programme was established in 2020 to grow and create awareness of the work of the Ombudsman among young people. Watch the video featuring our last year's interns, Charlotte Davis, Hinerangimarie Berryman and George Sabonadiere who share their internship journey with the Chief Ombudsman.

The Kiingitanga & Chief Ombudsman Summer Internship 2022/23

The Kiingitanga & Chief Ombudsman Summer Internship programme was established in August 2020 to raise awareness of the Chief Ombudsman's work among rangatahi Māori; and provide corporate work experience for Māori university students. We spoked to our last summer's Kiingitanga intern Hinerangimarie Berryman who shares her experience working with the Chief Ombudsman.
